## Attention as a practice

Attention is a practice rather than a resource that can simply be spent. The reader must decide what deserves sustained notice before starting an argument.

The author writes, "attention becomes durable when it is attached to a question". A reading session that begins with a question can separate evidence from decoration.

## A small method

The method has 3 steps: name the question, mark the evidence, and record what remains unresolved.

## Memory needs structure

Memory improves when notes preserve the relationship between a claim and its evidence. A summary without a source location becomes difficult to revisit.

The author writes, "a useful note keeps the path back to the passage". This chapter extends the first chapter's attention practice into a durable record.

## A compact record

A compact record names the chapter, the line range, and the unresolved question. It should not duplicate the entire source passage.
